version.changelog: Round 24: deep fragmentation analysis and redundancy governance

llm.summary: The skill matches its diagram-generation purpose, but it needs review because it sends diagram content to AnyGen, handles API keys, and instructs automatic dependency installation with limited scoping.

dimensions.detail: The requested read and exec tools are proportionate for a CLI integration, but users should expect local command execution, network access, and interaction with an external AnyGen service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The dependency installation guidance uses an auto-confirming anygen skill install command and later tells the agent to run an install command if the dependency is missing, but the command shown does not clearly pin the dependency name, source, version, or user confirmation boundary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are mostly task-focused, but they direct agents to submit user-provided diagram descriptions to a third-party renderer and do not clearly warn against sending confidential architecture, business process, personal data, or secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill recommends API key login and persistent environment-variable configuration; this is purpose-aligned for authentication, but command-line and environment exposure risks are only lightly addressed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to generate flowcharts and architecture diagrams through AnyGen CLI and www.anygen.io server-side rendering; that capability is coherent with the skill content and is repeatedly disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending diagram descriptions to AnyGen's service, avoid including secrets or confidential system details, handle API keys outside shared terminals and logs, and manually verify the dependency install target before allowing the agent to run the auto-confirming install command.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The remote rendering concern is supported by the artifact: server-side generation at www.anygen.io is core to the skill and disclosed, but the artifact does not give a clear privacy warning for sensitive diagram content.
[SQP-2] expected: The API-key concern is supported by the artifact: command-line and environment-variable key configuration are part of the documented auth flow, with only a limited warning to avoid leaking keys to version control.
